key_insight: Sparse, physics-constrained model discovery identifies interpretable isotropic yield and failure surfaces, with sharp Lode-angle dependence proving more valuable than many added terms.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports multiaxial failure-model calibration while addressing physical admissibility and reducing nominal-stress mapping bias through differentiable finite-element identification.
method: Compare sparse invariant libraries, extensions with cosine Lode modes and learnable PBP atoms, and mixtures of convex gauge experts.
Use a differentiable ray-wise first-root objective with admissibility penalties; competition-gated mixtures preserve convexity by construction.
Identify model structure and parameters directly from notched-bar loads via differentiable finite elements.
evidence_signal: Synthetic Mohr–Coulomb and PBP surfaces are recovered within 1% error; five experimental datasets are analysed, with PBP atoms yielding fourfold lower fitting error for concrete.
watch_item: Library-based models rely on admissibility penalties rather than guarantees, so fitted surfaces require careful convexity and re-entrant-branch checks.
paper_title: Sparse, admissible and interpretable: discovery of isotropic limit surfaces with extended invariant libraries, physically gated mixtures of experts, and end-to-end structural identification
